policy: Search this register and primary literature before admitting new work. Replication is useful only when it closes a named reproducibility or validation gap. These entries are not an exhaustive novelty search.

entries.title: Published fusion measurements and explicit power/energy accounting boundaries
entries.attribution: PPPL TFTR investigators; UKAEA/EUROfusion JET teams; LLNL/NIF and collaborators; UKAEA PROCESS for the separate Workbench models
entries.original_date: Selected physical experiments1994â€“2026; primary records checked16September2026
entries.classification: Attributed measurement-history consolidation and model-score presentation; no new experiment, solver or discovery
entries.our_status: Twelve computational history records and11 selected physical milestones retained with separate units, original-source links and qualification status.
entries.our_use: Make best conditional modeled net electricity and its limitations visible without ranking it against measured reaction energy or peak fusion power.
entries.already_known: MJ yield, peak fusion MW, mean reaction MW, target gain and net electric MW are distinct physical boundaries. The original experimental records belong to their investigators.
entries.do_not_repeat: Do not label the superseded406.53MW cross-study estimate as a coupled best result. Do not turn absent measurements into zero, NIF shot energy into continuous power, or a new report into a new power point.
entries.reopen_when: A new sourced experiment, corrected measurement statement, changed model result or qualification changes the records. Preserve non-record and rejected results.
entries.reading_scope: Primary laboratory/agency HTML statements; not raw experimental datasets or independent reproduction of the measurements.

entries.title: Established fixed-boundary Gradâ€“Shafranov construction; candidate interface checked
entries.attribution: Open FUSION Toolkit / TokaMaker original investigators and contributors; UKAEA PROCESS profile and systems authors; Workbench coupling/verification
entries.original_date: Existing TokaMaker method; official v26.6 example and v26.9 implementation reviewed
entries.classification: Reused numerical solver; new explicitly unqualified candidate construction and closure/refinement comparison
entries.our_status: Four completed current/pressure-energy-matched constructions; q95 mismatch persists under declared refinement; no candidate ray/current qualification.
entries.our_use: Map exact archived pressure shape through enclosed volume and test whether assumed scalar safety factors survive a force-balanced construction.
entries.already_known: Gradâ€“Shafranov solves, fixed-boundary profiles and mesh convergence are established. A prescribed boundary is not a PF-coil or plasma-stability demonstration.
entries.do_not_repeat: Do not repeat the earlier official DIII-D example as a new reactor result. Do not equate matching integrated current and energy with matching a full physical equilibrium.
entries.reopen_when: A physically substantiated diverted boundary/current/fast-pressure profile, numerical defect or new declared compatibility question changes the interface.
entries.reading_scope: Official example and installed26.9 source/API; no experimentally reconstructed candidate equilibrium was available.
entries.license_scope: Original Workbench coupling MIT; solver maintains upstream terms, no numerical library distribution.

entries.title: Established pulsed/current-drive trade-offs; candidate-specific power allocation test
entries.attribution: UKAEA PROCESS contributors; generic tokamak input by James Morris; Kembleton et al. EU-DEMO design-space work; EU-DEMO HCD contributors; Sugiyama, Aiba, Asakura, Hayashi and Sakamoto
entries.original_date: 2022 EU-DEMO studies;2024 JA-DEMO scenario study;2026 candidate-specific comparison
entries.classification: Reused existing methods; new conditional systems-design comparison, not experimental discovery
entries.our_status: Six bounded PROCESS solves completed: two steady-state failures and four pulsed points. Final controlled pair differs only in75vs30MW extra-heating allocation.
entries.our_use: Quantify useful power at fixed major radius using native output objective and unchanged drive/turbine efficiencies and constraints. Preserve all attempts and qualification gaps.
entries.already_known: Heating/current-drive, current-profile control and recirculating-power trade-offs already exist in reactor design literature. Systems-code feasibility is not integrated plasma validation.
entries.do_not_repeat: No generic steady-state demonstration or another scalar allocation sweep. Do not call the75MW heating-only pool wasted power; do not apply benchmark discrepancy factors or reuse old blanket results on altered geometry.
entries.reopen_when: A candidate-specific, substantiated deposition/control constraint, numerical defect or declared optimization-robustness question can change the design decision.
entries.reading_scope: Accessible publisher and contributing-author records, existing official PROCESS source. No reproduction of the papers' integrated plasma scenario models.
entries.license_scope: Original workbench integration MIT; referenced papers linked, not reproduced. Existing upstream PROCESS/input terms and credits retained.

entries.title: OKTAVIAN lithium-fluoride neutron leakage measurements
entries.attribution: Chihiro Ichihara, Shu A. Hayashi, Katsuhei Kobayashi, Itsuro Kimura, Junji Yamamoto, Mikio Izumi and Akito Takahashi; Kyoto University and Osaka University
entries.our_status: One-million-history transport replay completed; experiment agreement remains unqualified
entries.our_use: Compare frozen neutron/photon surface scores with an archived calculation and the IAEA-hosted neutron table, without fitting or dropping bins.
entries.already_known: These leakage experiments and transport-code comparisons predate this project by decades.
entries.do_not_repeat: Do not rebuild this benchmark or rerun identical histories as a discovery task; do not infer blanket breeding from LiF leakage.
entries.reopen_when: A documented normalization, measurement-response, source/nuclear-data or precision question can change an acceptance decision.
entries.reading_scope: Original authors'1988 abstract; exact pinned IAEA tables/input; OFB model/helper/archives; no claim to have read the full proceedings paper.
entries.license_scope: IAEA tabular data CC-BY-4.0; exact upstream notices retained; no paper fulltext redistributed.

entries.title: FNG HCPB lithium-carbonate / beryllium tritium benchmark
entries.attribution: P. Batistoni, P. Carconi, R. Villari, M. Angelone, M. Pillon and G. Zappa; ENEA experiment, as cited by JADE
entries.original_date: 2005 experiment and ENEA report;2006 consistency assessment
entries.classification: known more relevant experiment; not yet reproduced here
entries.our_status: Detailed public benchmark description located; complete usable input/data packet not acquired in this continuation
entries.our_use: Select the next qualification target because it measures tritium production in a lithium/beryllium assembly rather than leakage alone.
entries.already_known: Measurements and MCNP/OpenMC model descriptions exist; a new generic experiment is not required just to establish this validation question.
entries.do_not_repeat: Do not substitute aluminium or LiF leakage for tritium-production validation; do not invent pellet activity normalization or claim the documented model has been run.
entries.reopen_when: Complete geometry, source, pellet measurements, normalization and redistribution rights are available for a pinned reproduction.
entries.reading_scope: JADE description and NEA SINBAD NEA-1553/71 summary read; underlying experiment package and full original reports not obtained. The new OpenMC paper is recorded separately at abstract-level reading.

entries.title: Published OpenMC HCPB tritium benchmark and nuclear-data uncertainty study
entries.attribution: Felipe S. Novais and Ethan E. Peterson; Massachusetts Institute of Technology Plasma Science and Fusion Center
entries.original_date: Published online 23 October 2025; Fusion Science and Technology 82(4), 2026, pp.844-852
entries.classification: existing directly relevant validation study; not reproduced here
entries.our_status: Author/publisher abstract and metadata located; complete model, per-detector numerical data and uncertainty files not acquired here
entries.our_use: Replace the assumption that an OpenMC HCPB validation study must be invented. Seek the existing reproducible package before another model implementation.
entries.already_known: The authors compared OpenMC with MCNP-4C and SINBAD measurements for Li2CO3 pellets in a beryllium mock-up, including SANDY-based nuclear-data uncertainty; their abstract reports roughly9% mean tritium-production underprediction.
entries.do_not_repeat: Do not rebrand their benchmark or uncertainty method as a discovery. Do not multiply our candidate result by1/0.91, subtract9% from it, or treat9% as an uncertainty bound on our2.71% header contrast.
entries.reopen_when: The exact model/source version, pellet normalization, experimental uncertainties and reusable data terms are available for a declared independent reproduction or a demonstrated missing sensitivity test.
entries.reading_scope: Publisher and ANS abstract plus bibliographic metadata only; no full-text or per-detector data reproduction claimed.

entries.attribution: N. A. Lopez, A. Alieva, S. A. M. McNamara and X. Zhang
entries.classification: Existing method reviewed, not implemented or benchmarked here
